title: Career Roadmap · IT Support Engineer
summary: An IT Support Engineer helps individuals and organizations maintain reliable computer systems, networks, software, and IT equipment. The role involves troubleshooting technical issues, configuring devices, supporting users, maintaining IT assets, and escalating complex incidents to specialist teams.

blocks.text: An IT Support Engineer helps individuals and organizations maintain reliable computer systems, networks, software, and IT equipment. The role involves troubleshooting technical issues, configuring devices, supporting users, maintaining IT assets, and escalating complex incidents to specialist teams.

For a B.Voc graduate specializing in Cyber Security / Networking, this career provides a practical entry point into IT infrastructure, technical support, networking, systems administration, and cybersecurity operations.
Primary responsibilities

items.text: Diagnose and resolve computer, operating system, application, and peripheral issues.
Install, configure, and maintain desktop computers, laptops, printers, and business software.
Troubleshoot basic wired and wireless network connectivity problems.
Manage user accounts, passwords, permissions, and access requests according to policy.
Support Windows and, where required, Linux environments.
Record incidents, resolutions, and follow-up actions in a ticketing system.
Assist with software updates, antivirus protection, and endpoint security.
Support device setup, backups, and IT asset inventory.
Explain technical solutions clearly to non-technical users.
Escalate complex network, server, security, or hardware issues to the appropriate team.
Follow organizational procedures for data protection, security, and change management.

blocks.label: Primary objective
blocks.text: Restore IT services efficiently while protecting company systems, user data, and network security.

rows.text: Device setup, basic troubleshooting, and ticket documentation
User support, operating systems, hardware, and software issues
Incident resolution, endpoint management, and network troubleshooting
Complex incidents, mentoring, and infrastructure support
Servers, networks, access management, and infrastructure operations
IT Infrastructure Lead / Security Operations Specialist
Technical ownership, incident coordination, or security-focused operations

blocks.text: These are illustrative career horizons, not guaranteed timelines. Progression depends on practical troubleshooting ability, certifications, work experience, and employer requirements.
The following roadmap assumes a three-year B.Voc programme. Adapt it to the actual course duration and syllabus.
Year 1 — Computer Fundamentals and Technical Support

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Understand computer hardware, operating systems, basic networking, and user-support procedures.
Core subjects and concepts:

items.text: File systems, storage, and device drivers
LAN, WAN, Wi-Fi, routers, and switches

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Install an operating system in a lab environment.
Troubleshoot simulated printer and connectivity issues.
Practise basic commands such as ipconfig, ping, and tracert on Windows.
Document common problems and their solutions.

blocks.label: Year 1 outcome
blocks.text: Understand common IT components and perform basic troubleshooting in a controlled environment.
Year 2 — Networking, Systems Administration, and Security

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Develop practical skills for diagnosing network and endpoint issues.
Core subjects and concepts:

items.text: DHCP, DNS, gateways, and routing basics
Linux users, permissions, and basic services
Active Directory or equivalent identity-management concepts

blocks.text: Tools to learn:

items.text: Windows Settings, Device Manager, and Event Viewer
Windows command-line tools and PowerShell basics
VirtualBox or VMware for lab environments
A ticketing platform such as Jira Service Management or an equivalent tool

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Configure IP settings and troubleshoot DNS failures.
Create and manage test user accounts.
Analyse sample network traffic in a lab.
Practise installing updates and checking system logs.
Create a simulated help-desk ticket queue.

blocks.label: Year 2 outcome
blocks.text: Troubleshoot routine desktop and network issues, document incidents, and understand essential security controls.
Year 3 — Enterprise Support and Job Readiness

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Prepare for real-world IT support by practising service management, endpoint administration, troubleshooting, and security-aware operations.
Core subjects and concepts:

items.text: IT service management and incident handling

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Set up a Windows and Linux virtual lab.
Create a troubleshooting handbook for common IT issues.
Simulate user onboarding, account changes, and offboarding.
Create a ticket dashboard tracking resolution time and recurring incidents.
Complete an internship in help desk, desktop support, networking, or IT operations.

blocks.label: Year 3 outcome
blocks.text: Demonstrate structured troubleshooting, professional ticket documentation, basic infrastructure administration, and security-aware support practices.

rows.text: IP addressing, DNS, DHCP, gateways, and Wi-Fi
Files, permissions, processes, and command-line tools
Identify, isolate, test, resolve, and document issues
Accounts, authentication, permissions, and access requests
Basic administration and repetitive task automation
Incident, request, problem, and change concepts
Install, configure, and troubleshoot common issues
Manage users, permissions, files, and services
Automate simple checks and administrative tasks
Inspect traffic in an authorized lab
Record, prioritize, resolve, and escalate tickets
Understand alerts, updates, and basic response procedures
Model basic networks and troubleshoot configurations

blocks.text: Tool availability and employer environments vary. Start with a reliable virtual lab and learn the platforms most common in the vacancies you target.
Complete at least four projects and document the problem, diagnostic steps, resolution, and verification process.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: IT Help Desk Knowledge Base

items.text: Select 15–20 common issues, such as slow computers, printer problems, and Wi-Fi disconnections.
Include resolution instructions and verification checks.
Specify when an issue should be escalated.
Use clear language for non-technical users.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A structured troubleshooting guide.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Virtual Network Troubleshooting Lab

items.text: Simulate DNS, gateway, and connectivity problems.
Use ping, tracert or traceroute, and ipconfig or equivalent tools.
Document the root cause and resolution of each scenario.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A network diagram and troubleshooting report.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Windows and Linux Administration Lab

items.text: Practise backup and restoration with non-sensitive test files.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A system administration workbook with screenshots if permitted by your course or lab.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Ticket Management Dashboard

items.text: Categorize issues by type, priority, and status.
Track response time and resolution time.
Build a dashboard using Excel or Power BI.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A ticket report with recommendations for reducing recurring incidents.

blocks.label: Project 5
blocks.text: Security-Aware Endpoint Checklist

items.text: Create a checklist for updates, antivirus status, screen locking, backups, and access permissions.
Use a test machine or authorized lab.
Document potential risks and escalation requirements.
Include a change record for any configuration adjustments.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: An endpoint hygiene checklist and a sample audit report.
Never test against systems, networks, or user accounts without authorization. Use virtual machines and intentionally vulnerable lab environments for security practice.

rows.text: Diagnoses common peripheral and device issues
Diagnoses routine IP, DNS, DHCP, and Wi-Fi issues
Maintains complete incident records and escalation details
Follows access, patching, and incident-escalation procedures
Handles basic accounts, permissions, and device configuration
Writes or adapts simple PowerShell scripts safely

blocks.text: Prioritize internships that provide hands-on exposure to desktop support, networks, operating systems, and enterprise IT processes.
Potential employers and work settings:

items.text: IT services and managed service providers
Banking and financial services IT teams
Data centres and infrastructure service providers
Small businesses with internal IT operations

blocks.text: Useful internship search terms:
During an internship, seek opportunities to work with ticketing systems, device configuration, user onboarding, network diagnostics, asset inventory, and incident documentation.

rows.text: Troubleshoots user devices, applications, and basic network issues
Supports computers, peripherals, and business applications
Diagnoses product or system issues for users or clients
Assists with connectivity and network troubleshooting
Supports routine infrastructure and system operations
Assists with account, device, and server administration
Supports device configuration, patching, and endpoint tools

blocks.text: Job titles and responsibilities vary by organization. Some employers may require shift work, customer-service experience, specific operating-system knowledge, or relevant certifications.

rows.text: Documented case studies for common IT issues
A lab network diagram and diagnostic report
Sample ticket responses and user-friendly instructions
Ticket workflow with priorities and escalation rules
Endpoint security checklist and safe lab practices
Internship experience or a documented group project
Complete records, change notes, and resolution verification

blocks.text: Choose certifications that align with your desired entry-level role and available budget.
Recommended learning areas:
Potential certification pathways include:

blocks.label: CompTIA A+
blocks.text: Hardware, operating systems, troubleshooting, and IT support fundamentals.

blocks.label: CompTIA Network+
blocks.text: Networking concepts and troubleshooting.

blocks.label: Cisco CCST Networking
blocks.text: Entry-level networking knowledge.

blocks.label: Cisco CCST Cybersecurity
blocks.text: Foundational cybersecurity concepts.

blocks.label: ITIL Foundation
blocks.text: IT service management concepts.

blocks.label: Microsoft Learn
blocks.text: Windows, Microsoft 365, identity, and endpoint-management learning paths.

Certification names, exam requirements, prices, and availability can change. Check the providers' official websites before registering. A certificate is useful, but hands-on labs and the ability to explain your troubleshooting process are equally important.
Depending on eligibility and career goals, possible next steps include:

items.text: PG Diploma in Networking or Systems Administration
Further study in computer science or information technology, where eligible

blocks.text: A postgraduate qualification is not always required for entry-level support roles. Practical troubleshooting, networking fundamentals, communication, and relevant certifications can be sufficient for many junior positions.
Desktop and Endpoint Support
Specialize in user devices, operating systems, software deployment, endpoint configuration, and troubleshooting.
Networking and Infrastructure
Develop skills in switching, routing, DNS, DHCP, Wi-Fi, network monitoring, and infrastructure support.
Cybersecurity Operations
Progress toward endpoint security, access management, security monitoring, and incident response.
Systems Administration
Focus on user accounts, servers, system updates, backups, permissions, and service availability.
Cloud and SaaS Support
Support cloud productivity platforms, identity services, user access, and cloud-based applications.

items.text: AI-assisted IT service desks and ticket classification
Cloud infrastructure and hybrid IT environments

blocks.text: AI-powered tools may assist with ticket summaries, knowledge-base searches, and routine diagnostics. Engineers must still verify recommendations, protect sensitive data, and follow approved change-management procedures.
By graduation, aim to demonstrate:

blocks.label: Hardware
blocks.text: Computer components, peripherals, and basic diagnostics.

blocks.label: Operating systems
blocks.text: Windows support and Linux fundamentals.

blocks.label: Networking
blocks.text: IP addressing, DNS, DHCP, Wi-Fi, and connectivity troubleshooting.

blocks.label: Troubleshooting
blocks.text: Structured diagnosis, resolution verification, and escalation.

blocks.label: Service management
blocks.text: Ticket documentation, prioritization, and incident handling.

blocks.label: Security
blocks.text: Access control, patching, endpoint protection, and safe data handling.

blocks.label: Administration
blocks.text: User accounts, permissions, software installation, and device setup.

blocks.label: Automation
blocks.text: Basic PowerShell commands and scripts.

blocks.label: Communication
blocks.text: Clear technical explanations and user support.

blocks.label: Portfolio
blocks.text: At least four documented lab projects and a troubleshooting knowledge base.

A graduate ready to apply for an IT Support Engineer role should be able to troubleshoot common desktop and connectivity problems, configure operating systems and user accounts, understand basic networking, manage support tickets, document resolutions, and follow security procedures.

blocks.label: Best overall positioning
blocks.text: Combine Windows support + networking fundamentals + troubleshooting + ticket management + cybersecurity awareness. This offers a practical entry route into IT support while creating a foundation for later specialization in networking, systems administration, cloud support, or cybersecurity.
